News.title: Drug gangs exploited and raped us as teens, then police failed us, women tell BBC
News.content:
Warning: Contains details of sexual exploitation

"It was the thrill of being with a bad boy."

Christine was 13 when she began exchanging messages online with someone she believed was a teenage boy.

On their first meeting, she discovered he was a grown man 10 years older than herself. He also told her he was involved with gangs and drugs.

"I always knew, OK, he's probably hurt someone, but in terms of hurting me, I didn't think it would get to that point," she says.

Over the next few years, he would use Christine to courier drugs, subject her to extreme sexual exploitation, and assault her so violently she feared she might die.

Christine is one of four women who have chosen to waive their anonymity and speak publicly to the BBC documentary, Britain's Forgotten Girls, about how they were targeted by criminals when they were children.

Their stories, covering 2002 to last year, differ in detail - but reveal strikingly similar patterns of abuse. All four describe being targeted by boys and older men connected to drug gangs, manipulated into abusive relationships, then repeatedly sexually exploited.

All believe the authorities failed to protect them and did not take their allegations seriously.

The sexual and criminal exploitation of girls by drug gangs has long been overshadowed in public discussion by the focus on sexual grooming gangs, according to front-line social workers and experts in the field.

"For grooming gangs, the primary purpose is often the sexual exploitation of those girls, but the primary purpose of a drug gang is to make money off selling drugs and other criminal activity," says Connie Muttock from the children's charity, Centre for Young Lives.

Girls are brought in to generate money, says Muttock, but many are also sexually abused by gang members.

News.title: Learner drivers still forced to wait months to book tests
News.content:
Learner drivers have to wait an average 20 weeks, or around five months, before booking a practical test, according to new figures, despite attempts to reduce delays.

The data from the Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency (DVSA) for August is only a marginal improvement from 20.2 weeks in July.

The average wait time between booking and sitting a test is unchanged at 11.1 weeks.

The DVSA initially had a target of reducing the average waiting time to seven weeks by the end of last year. Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander pushed the target back to summer 2026, but subsequently admitted even that would not be possible.

The DVSA made a number of changes to its practical driving test booking system earlier this year.

Only the learner driver themself is now able to book their driving test, blocking an instructor or third parties from booking using the learner's details.

There is also a geographical restriction which means a learner can only book a test at their three local test centres, rather than one at the other side of the country if they found a test available.

The number of times a would-be driver can swap a test date has also been restricted.

News.title: Divorcing abusive husband cost woman £105k
News.content:
A woman who endured years of abusive controlling behaviour by her ex-husband says it has cost her more than Â£105,000 to divorce him.

Annabelle Boucher, 48, from Somerset, wants the law changed after she paid Â£75,000 to David Rogers, 61, despite him admitting to coercive and controlling behaviour. She also had to pay her legal costs.

"I thought being stuck in this relationship I couldn't get out of would be highlighted within the divorce procedure," Boucher said. "But the divorce law doesn't take into account the fact that he was a criminal."

The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) said it had begun a consultation to reform the law so "family courts meet the needs of domestic abuse victims".

Boucher, a mother from Chiselborough, said Rogers had come into her life in "a whirlwind" in 2017 and the pair got married two years later.

It was once they were married that things started to "take a turn", she said, and "some very extreme behaviour started to happen".

"It creeps up on you and you're in it, and so you don't kind of notice what is happening."

Boucher said she had ended up "shutting down emotionally" and "cutting off from everyone" because she feared what would happen.

"You find that you're trapped within a situation that you can't get out of."

News.title: Channel 4 to cut 340 jobs by the end of the year in major shake-up
News.content:
Channel 4 has said it plans to cut 340 jobs before the end of the year, reducing its workforce by more than a quarter.

The network, which broadcasts Gogglebox and The Great British Bake Off, will lose around 28% of its current 1,270 staff following a strategic review of the organisation.

Priya Dogra, Channel 4's chief executive, said the announcement "marks the first phase of our transformation, ensuring Channel 4 is the right shape and size to deliver its future strategy and focus investment in the programmes audiences love".

Caroline Dinenage, chair of the culture, media and sport committee said the news would be "deeply worrying for the talented and dedicated people who work at Channel 4".

The network said it planned to focus on creating a simpler and more efficient operating model and enable greater investment in distinctive programming.

In her statement, Dogra said: "Channel 4 is a precious asset which plays a unique role in the UK.

"We need to secure and own our future so we can continue to make shows others won't, reach audiences others can't, and thrive as a distinctive and disruptive British voice for future generations.

"The challenges we face require a fundamental transformation in how we work. I know the proposals we are announcing today will be very difficult for many colleagues and will have a significant impact across the organisation."

She added: "These decisions have not been taken lightly, but I strongly believe they are necessary to create a simpler, more focused and more sustainable Channel 4."

A Jersey Shore town and its police department are being sued after allegedly letting an 11-year-old operate a golf cart while wearing drunk-driving “impairment goggles” — which the youngster crashed into a crowd.

The incident unfolded on August 6, 2024, in Wildwood, along the New Jersey coast, during a community event known as National Night Out, meant to foster relations between residents and local police officers.

Children in attendance could navigate a course on a golf cart while wearing “impairment goggles” that simulate intoxication. An 11-year-old was participating when he pressed the accelerator pedal and lost control of the vehicle, The Philadelphia Inquirer reported.

The golf cart veered off the course, which had been set up with orange police cones on a baseball field at Fox Park, and injured several people.

Wildwood police officer Jonathan Goraj was in the passenger seat of the golf cart at the time of the incident, according to a lawsuit filed August 5, 2026, in Cape May County Superior Court.

open image in gallery Wildwood, New Jersey, is being sued after allegedly allowing an 11-year-old boy operate a golf cart while wearing ‘impairment goggles’ that simulate drunk driving, according to a report ( Getty Images )

Wildwood resident Christopher Hines and his extended family from Ohio — David and Lori Galambos, their daughter Rachel Kelly, and their grandsons, Simon and Gideon — are named as plaintiffs in the suit.

The lawsuit alleges that the police officer and department should have known the risk of putting a child in the driver’s seat while simulating intoxication “because the very purpose of the demonstration was to illustrate the dangers of impaired driving.”

Hines, David Galambos and Simon Galambos were injured in the crash, while the mom, grandmother and sibling witnessed it, the lawsuit claims.

Hines suffered injuries to his neck, back and legs, while the grandfather suffered injuries to his neck, rib, hip and “severe emotional trauma,” the lawsuit states.

open image in gallery Three people, including the child, were injured in the crash ( Getty Images )

Simon, the child, suffered a collapsed lung, a concussion and injuries to his neck and back. He also suffered from emotional distress, the lawsuit said.

The defendants in the suit are the City of Wildwood, its police department, Goraj and the National Night Out organization.

A city spokesperson said they do not comment on open litigation.

Martin Lewis’s charity has launched a new project aimed at transforming the support banks and building societies provide to customers who may be feeling suicidal.

The Money and Mental Health Policy Institute stated it will support Barclays, HSBC, Lloyds, Monzo and Nationwide Building Society in collaborating to test new approaches, aiming to identify effective methods and lead improvements in support.

The announcement was timed to coincide with World Suicide Prevention Day.

The organisation highlighted that banks have a crucial opportunity because of their unique insights into personal finances, allowing them to step in when customers face debt issues or falling incomes.

The "action lab" will utilise insights from individuals, research by Money and Mental Health, and guidance from a steering group including the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).

The Money and Mental Health Policy Institute will support banks like HSBC in testing new methods of support for those who are suicidal ( Reuters )

Money and Mental Health will publish the full outcomes of these pilot schemes in the summer of 2028.

Mr Lewis, founder and chair of the Money and Mental Health Policy Institute, said: “The link between mental health difficulties and debt is a marriage made in hell – they feed off and cause each other.

“Long-term money worries grind people down, and aggressive debt collection practices can leave them feeling completely hopeless.

“Banks didn’t cause all these problems, but they are in a unique central position in people’s financial lives, and we want to see if it’s possible to take advantage of that to be able to spot when customers are in trouble and urgently direct them to the right support.

“So I’m delighted and thankful so many major banks have committed to working with Money and Mental Health on our new suicide prevention action lab.”

Mr Lewis added: “We aim to get under the bonnet with banks to find the gaps, test new ways to identify and support people in crisis, and drive change not just with those who’ve signed up but right across the sector – and potentially save lives.”

Economic Secretary to the Treasury Lucy Rigby said: “Financial worries and mental health challenges too often go hand in hand.

“I have seen first-hand how the industry can make a real difference to people’s lives through concerted action and I am very hopeful that this excellent project will help us find new ways to support people before they reach crisis point.”

Alison McGovern, Minister of State for Mental Health, said: “The suicide prevention action lab has the potential to make a real difference in identifying and supporting vulnerable people who are at risk of suicide, and save many lives over the coming years.”

The Samaritans charity, which offers support to people who are struggling, said earlier this week it wanted to let people know that suicidal thoughts “can be interrupted” by other people – and that rather than being concerned with saying “the perfect thing”, it is better just ask if someone is okay.

If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI), email jo@samaritans.org, or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch.

If you are based in the USA, and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call or text 988, or visit 988lifeline.org to access online chat from the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week.If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you

Despite endless speculation about the new hosts of Strictly Come Dancing, the news that Johannes Radebe, Josh Widdicombe and Emma Willis were taking over was still met with genuine shock.

And now the trio, who are replacing long-time Strictly hosts Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman as the dance competition returns this month, have opened up about the extreme lengths the BBC went to keep their identities secret.

Speaking to Richard Osman on The Rest is Entertainment podcast, Radebe, 39, Widdicombe, 43, and Willis, 50, revealed that the Strictly team came up with a fictitious TV show that they should pretend to be trying out for while they were auditioning.

The process was so secretive it felt “a bit like [The] Traitors”, former Big Brother presenter Willis explained, as she revealed that the trio were individually asked to come in for chemistry tests only to be picked up in cars not knowing the location.

open image in gallery From L-R: New ‘Strictly’ presenters Radebe, Willis and Widdicombe ( PA )

Widdicombe said that the trio had been respectively told to keep secret what they were actually auditioning for, as the driver had been told that he was bringing them in to try out for a gardening show.

The comedian then explained that the production team had gone as far as to name this fictitious programme, calling it The Great Garden Glow Up.

“They created a whole new name for a show for the cab drivers,” Willis said.

Widdicombe then joked: “I did feel like saying to my agent, ’I wouldn’t have gone to The Great Garden Glow Up chemistry test.’”

“I am in the back of the car and there is a cabbie who is judging me, because he thinks I would present a show called The Great Garden Glow Up,” riffed back Osman.

open image in gallery Comedian Widdicombe recalled the extreme lengths the BBC went to to keep the show's casting a secret ( Getty )

Willis then explained that the trio individually arrived at the studio to find a mock studio set-up, complete with camera crew and members of the production team who were acting as stand-ins for the judges.

“We’re literally going to pretend to do Strictly,” she explained, with Widdicombe adding: ”Shout out to the producer who did the best Craig Revel Horwood impression I’ve ever seen.”

The presenting trio will be at the helm as Strictly returns for its 24th series this month, with the launch show airing on 19 September when the celebrity contestants will meet their professional partners for the first time.

The pro dancers, like the presenting team, have also seen a major shake-up this series; many fan-favourites have left the show, with five new dancers joining the cast.

The first live show will then take place on 26 September, during which all 15 contestants will dance in front of the public for the first time.

Duran Duran’s almost five-decade journey from the Birmingham club scene to international acclaim is being celebrated by Royal Mail through a new set of special stamps focused on their album artwork.

The collection also features a miniature sheet centred around their tour posters from the 1980s until the 2020s, serving as a visual timeline of their live performances over the years.

Formed in 1978, the award-winning group are famed for tracks such as Rio, Hungry Like The Wolf and Ordinary World, having secured two UK number one singles and a chart-topping album.

Lead vocalist Simon Le Bon praised the new release, describing the set as "a massive visual validation of the band and its history" and a "pinch yourself" moment.

He added that he feels "so happy and fortunate" to be part of the band’s lasting legacy.

open image in gallery Simon Le Bon said the release of the stamps was a ‘pinch yourself’ moment ( Royal Mail )

Discussing what the new collection means to the band, Le Bon said: “Having stamps is a bit far out. Nobody would have anticipated this at any time.

“For so many years, we were struggling against the negativity. We’re not a flash in the pan, and the stamps really vindicate us.

“It’s big stuff. It’s a massive visual validation of the band and its history.”

The 67-year-old continued: “When you see those album covers all lined up, all eight of them, you look at it say, ‘we’ve done a lot of work’.

“And we’ve done it together – we’ve stayed together – and it reminds us of that. I just feel so happy and fortunate to be part of all that.”

The singer joined the group in 1980 and is a core part of its current line-up, alongside keyboardist Nick Rhodes, bassist John Taylor and drummer Roger Taylor.

open image in gallery Nick Rhodes described the stamps as ‘mini masterpieces’ ( Royal Mail )

Rhodes said it is a “real honour” to be represented on British stamps and told PA: “We’re proud as a band that we’re even still around all these years later, but we keep finding little things like this that happen that make everything even more surprising and special.”

Fellow founder John described the collaboration as “a Duran Duran legacy project”, while Roger said it makes the band feel like it is “part of the cultural furniture” in the country.

“The band is almost set in stone now. Once you start getting things like this, there’s an immortality,” Roger added.

The new stamp collection includes eight album covers spanning records such as Duran Duran, Rio, Seven And The Raged Tiger, Notorious, Duran Duran (The Wedding Album), Astronaut Paper Gods and Future Past.

“I think it was great that we picked the album covers rather than beauty shots or shots of us, because the legacy is the music,” Le Bon said.

“I think the fans will be really proud.”

Rhodes described the stamps as “mini masterpieces”, and added: “From the moment I was born I was looking at Royal Mail stamps.

“I was excited when letters arrived at home through the letterbox.

“I still am – so to be a little part of that is magical, and just the greatest honour.”

The group have become the ninth music band to feature in a Royal Mail stamp issue, joining The Beatles, Pink Floyd, Queen, The Rolling Stones, Iron Maiden, Spice Girls, The Who and AC/DC.

The release of their stamps coincide with the 45th anniversary of their debut album Duran Duran and its breakthrough single Planet Earth, which peaked at number 12 on the UK singles chart.

The stamps, and a range of collectable products, are available to pre-order from September 10 and go on general sale from September 17.

The UK property market is showing signs of stabilising as declines in both buyer demand and sales eased during August, according to industry surveyors.

Data from the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (Rics) reveals that a net balance of 19% of property professionals reported a drop in new buyer inquiries rather than an increase.

While buyer interest remains in negative territory, the figure represents the fifth consecutive monthly improvement and the least pessimistic reading recorded since January, the monthly report noted.

Similarly, agreed sales saw a net balance of 17% reporting a decline—the least negative reading since February, and a notable rebound from April's low when a balance of 38% reported falling transactions.

Sales expectations for the upcoming three months moved closer to neutral ground, with a net balance of 3% anticipating a reduction in activity, compared to 13% who expected a fall in July.

Looking further ahead over the next 12 months, a positive net balance of 6% of professionals now forecast higher sales volumes, up from 3% in the previous survey, pointing to a modest recovery in broader market confidence.

House prices remained under downward pressure, Rics said, with a net balance of 28% of professionals seeing falls, compared with a net balance of 29% seeing price falls in July.

This indicates a gradual improvement from April’s net balance of 35%.

London’s price balance remained more negative than the average, although it improved on July, Rics said.

Falls in home buyer demand and sales were less sharp in August than in recent months, in signs of the market becoming more stable, according to surveyors.

A net balance of 19% of property professionals saw new buyer inquiries fall rather than rise, the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (Rics) said.

While home buyer inquiries appear to be dropping, it is the least negative reading recorded since January and the fifth improvement in a row, according to the monthly report.

A net balance of 17% of property professionals saw a fall in agreed sales, which was the least negative reading since February and an improvement from April’s low of a balance of 38% of professionals who reported sales sliding.

Expectations for sales over the next three months also moved closer to neutral territory, with a net balance of 3% of professionals expecting a fall, improving from a balance of 13% in July who expected to see sales decrease.

Looking 12 months ahead, a positive net balance of 6% of professionals predict higher sales volumes, compared with 3% previously, also pointing to a modest improvement in confidence.

House prices remained under downward pressure, Rics said, with a net balance of 28% of professionals seeing falls, compared with a net balance of 29% seeing price falls in July.

This indicates a gradual improvement from April’s net balance of 35%.

London’s price balance remained more negative than the average, although it improved on July, Rics said.

News.title: Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal
News.content:
In five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

“That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”

In the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

“With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” said Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”

News.title: Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea
News.content:
Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

Alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

When it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”

News.title: Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner
News.content:
Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

News.title: Gay does enough to earn another chance as England dominate again
News.content:
There are two places up for grabs in England’s top three and three players vying: Gay, Jordan Cox and Jacob Bethell, who spent the day on the players’ balcony dropping a reminder of his looming return. A hundred for Durham by Ben McKinney, the one challenger outside of the squad, tweaked the ante up further.

One of Cox or Gay will make way for Bethell when England begin their next series in Johannesburg on December 17, which will be the first Test of the Stephen Fleming era and the first big call he has to make. Cox was on the up after scores of 75 at Headingley and 55 in the first innings at Lord’s, looking the part at No 3. Gay’s luck had run out with a grubber in the second Test and he wasted a couple of 30s in other innings. Cox has opened in first-class cricket and Bethell could also take on the role of Ben Duckett’s partner. The squeeze was on.

But Cox perhaps got a little ahead of himself and played what could be a costly, impetuous shot at Mohammad Abbas to fall for six and hand Gay a chance. Neither Cox nor Gay have been tested on the back foot by genuine pace which will happen at the Wanderers in December but their performances have to be judged against the backdrop of a seam bowlers’ summer. Gay is averaging 27.1 from 10 innings, a number probably worth another 10 runs given the conditions.

His dismissal 20 minutes before the close, playing on driving away from his body, was the one time his footwork was non-existent and Razaullah deserved the breakthrough for coming back and hitting 90mph after tea following so little first-class cricket and a rushed call-up amidst the bloodletting.

News.title: Apple launches its first foldable iPhone – plus other key reveals from the launch
News.content:
Unlike previous Apple launches, the standard iPhone 18 model is due to be revealed at a later date. Reports indicate that it will release early next year.

The Wednesday showcase instead focused on the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models. Aside from the price, the only difference between the two versions is size: the Pro has a 6.3-inch screen, while the Pro Max has a 6.9-inch display.

Both phones have a smaller and less intrusive “Dynamic Island” selfie camera cutout at the top of the screen compared to older models. And like the iPhone Duo, they are powered by Apple’s latest A20 Pro chip, which should be up to 40 per cent faster than the previous iPhone 17 Pro.

The biggest change is with the camera system. The main camera now features a “variable aperture”, which allows you to manually adjust the amount of light passing through the lens, much like a regular camera. This means you should get better nighttime images with extra detail and more control.

Apple says that the 18 Pro Max has the longest-lasting battery life of any iPhone to date, thanks to a new internal heat management system, revamped battery design and efficiencies with the new A20 Pro chip. Battery life is quoted at 36 hours for the 18 Pro when playing video, and 45 hours for the 18 Pro Max. It also charges faster, providing 50 per cent charge after just 15 minutes plugged in.

Elsewhere, the colour-matched aluminium and back glass comes in two new colour choices: burgundy and blue, alongside black and silver.

Both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are more expensive than last year’s models. The 18 Pro costs £1,199 (a £100 increase), while the 18 Pro Max starts at £1,299. Rival smartphone firm Samsung raised the price of its Galaxy S26 Ultra by £30 earlier this year.

This change aligns with Apple recently raising prices of the iPad and MacBook by up to £300. At the time, CEO Tim Cook said that the price increases were due to the soaring costs of memory chips, which are in high demand thanks to the AI data centre boom.

News.title: Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double
News.content:
Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

Team news from Portugal to follow shortly.

News.title: Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start
News.content:
Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he said.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

Sports.title: Moment mass brawl erupts at Sunday League football match with players throwing punches as game descends into violence
Sports.content:
A VIOLENT football brawl spilled into A&E when a man allegedly stormed into hospital and attacked medics treating casualties from the scrap.

Shocking footage captures players and others trading savage blows after a Sunday league match erupted into chaos.



Spectators can be seen ducking under a makeshift rope barrier separating the players from the pitch before piling into the fray.

Within seconds, large groups of men and women are seen charging onto the pitch as the row erupts into a chaotic mass scrap.



The wounded were then rushed into the nearby emergency department, triggering a frantic scramble as every available member of staff battled to cope with the sudden surge.

But the mayhem allegedly followed them through the hospital doors.

One man is accused of barging into the emergency unit, hurling abuse and assaulting healthcare workers before cops were called to bring the situation under control.

The original violence erupted on a sports pitch beside the community hospital in Bulnes, Chile, on Sunday, September 6, according to creatorzine.com.

The Ñuble Health Service and bosses at Bulnes Community Family Health Hospital have since condemned the shocking scenes.

In a joint statement, they voiced their “absolute rejection of any form of violence against health workers” following the alleged attack inside the emergency department.



Officials said treatment continued despite the turmoil “thanks to the commitment and professionalism of the teams”.

Authorities are now preparing to file a criminal complaint against the person accused of attacking hospital staff.

The clubs involved have not been named and officials have not revealed how many people were hurt in the football brawl.



It remains unclear whether anyone involved in the initial clash was arrested.

Anyone with footage or information about the explosive incident has been urged to contact police.

It comes after a Colombia football game was suspended for almost an hour after fans invaded the pitch to brawl with sticks and chairs.

The top flight clash between Santa Fe and America de Cali on Saturday had to be halted after chaotic scenes involving supporters.

Violence initially broke out in the stands midway through the first half as fans from both sides scrapped over claims that one group had their flag stolen.



Fighting then spilled out onto the pitch at the El Campin stadium in Bogota and a mass brawl erupted.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis sacks his 25TH manager in 16 years just seven games into club’s season
Sports.content:
EVANGELOS MARINAKIS has sacked his 25TH manager in just 16 years just seven games into the season.

The Nottingham Forest owner is also the boss of Greek giants Olympiacos and Portuguese side Rio Ave.



The club have announced that manager Jose Luis Mendilibar has left his role in the dugout.

Mendilibar, 65, had led the club to a Conference League triumph in 2024 before winning a domestic treble the following season.



But after failing to qualify for the Champions League this season a change in manager has been made.

Olympiacos confirmed the decision with a statement which honoured his achievements.

It then went on to state that his time at the club was over.

A segment said: “But in football, as in life, there are cycles that eventually close. But what resonates in eternity is what you have achieved.

“The appreciation, respect and love of the OLYMPIC family will accompany you forever, General, along with the strong emotions that united us and are eternal.

“Thank you for everything.”

Former Burnley and Everton boss Sean Dyche was then hired before getting in the firing line after 25 games.



The East Midlands side survived relegation with Vítor Pereira in charge but the club parted with him after the season ended.

Oliver Glasner has since taken charge at the City Ground following his exit from Crystal Palace.

The club is currently third in the Greek Super League after three games in which they have won two and drawn one.

Sports.title: Fans realise what Marcos Llorente named his dog as he torments Liverpool again – and Steven Gerrard makes cheeky quip
Sports.content:
FANS have discovered that Atletico Madrid star Marcos Llorente has named his dog Anfield.

The pet’s cheeky name is another dig as the 31-year-old continues to torment Liverpool.



Llorente opted to name his pug after the iconic Premier League stadium after knocking Liverpool out of the Champions League in 2020.

He bagged a brace as Atletico secured a 3-2 win in extra-ime to march into the quarter-finals of the European competition.



While the Spanish side ultimately fell 2-1 against RB Leipzig in the following round, Anfield has remained a happy hunting ground for Llorente.

Llorente bagged another brace against Liverpool during last season’s Champions League group stage.

This was followed by a fifth Anfield goal in the 17th minute of Atletico’s opening-round visit to Merseyside during this season’s campaign.

The defender’s pug’s name has led several fans on social media to note Llorente’s “special connection” with Anfield.

Sports.title: Iraola gives update on Bradley Barcola after £123m Liverpool signing suffers worrying-looking injury in first start
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL have cause for concern as new £123million signing Bradley Barcola was subbed off with an injury in their win over Atletico Madrid.

The Reds came back to beat the Spanish giants 2-1 thanks to goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister cancelling out Marcos Llorente‘s opener.



But Barcola was withdrawn just before the hour mark after clutching his left calf.

The Frenchman was replaced by fellow summer recruit Victor Munoz, but boss Andoni Iraola has offered fans hope he won’t be out for long.



Speaking to Steven Gerrard and TNT Sports after the game, the Spaniard suggested the electrifying winger thought it might be cramp.

Laura Woods noticing Barcola mouthed “cramp” to the manager as he exited the pitch, with the former Bournemouth boss patting him on the back as was replaced.

Iraola said: “I just asked him if it was cramp and he said yes, so that was a relief.

“It was just cramp. We have been rushing Bradley a little bit because he hadn’t played any minutes in pre-season.

“We wanted him to play but said to just give us whatever he had. We have another game in three days.”

Barcola was walking about on the pitch after the game embracing his team-mates and the opposition, seemingly OK.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

It capped a frustrating night for the French international after he went clean through on goal and failed to even hit the target.

He dragged the effort wide and many fans might feel for £123m, you have to score those chances.

It was Barcola’s first start for the club after he played the last 26 minutes of their 2-0 victory over Ipswich at the weekend.

But he is clearly still getting up to speed after not doing much of PSG’s pre-season prior to his move.

Iraola seems to be optimistic that it won’t be too bad and to see him walking around the pitch at the end suggests it should not be a bad one.

Sports.title: Chelsea 6 Leeds 3: Cole Palmer climbs off the bench to spark barnstorming comeback in nine-goal Carabao Cup thriller
Sports.content:
MORGAN ROGERS delivered a hat-trick of assists as Xabi Alonso’s cavalry rescued Chelsea from a Carabao Cup nightmare.

Alonso hit the panic button at half-time, with the Blues 1-0 down thanks to goals from Tarik Murahemovic, only for Leeds to score again moments later through Brenden Aaronson.



But his super-subs sparked a comeback, firing four goals in 11 crazy minutes to eventually seal a 5-3 thriller at Stamford Bridge.

Alonso gambled early, starting 16-year-old Reggie Watson – Chelsea’s fourth-youngest player ever – while resting his ‘CPR’ frontline of Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro, and Rogers.



By the break, the Blues were flatlining and desperately needed resuscitation.

Enter Dr. Palmer.



The first half was a tale of two teams, as Leeds looked gritty and ruthless, while Chelsea’s expensive show-ponies were all stepovers and no substance.

Young Blues keeper Mike Penders produced two stunning saves to keep Leeds at bay, but was powerless when £34million defender Murahemovic nodded home Harry Wilson’s deep corner, which left new set piece coach Austin MacPhee practically spitting his words into the Stamford Bridge turf.

Danny Welbeck saw a golden chance blocked by Jaka Bijol before Alonso’s disjointed side trudged down the tunnel to a chorus of groans from players and fans alike.

The Blues were all bark and no bite, until Alonso unleashed the big dogs.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Throwing on Palmer, Rogers, Reece James, and Pedro Neto felt more like a hope and a prayer than a masterstroke from Alonso, but it was a prayer that was answered – with a slight delay…

Ex-Blues academy kid Ethan Ampadu tore down the right early in the second half, feeding Lukas Nmecha to flick past Maxence Lacroix for Brenden Aaronson to tap home.

It felt like game over, until Cole Palmer stepped up to the penalty spot.

Daniel James clumsily felled Pep Chavarria in the box, and Palmer coolly converted the 53rd-minute penalty before wheeling off in celebration with his trademark shivering move.

Just two minutes later, he stroked a silky half-volley into the bottom corner to level the scoring.



Neto fired home a third to complete the turnaround, before Rogers grabbed his treble of assists by teeing up Welbeck to nutmeg new Leeds keeper Michael Zetterer for number four.

Leeds tried to mount a late comeback when Calvert Lewin found the back of the net with 15 minutes to go, but the Blues shut them down once again.

World Cup villain Valentin Barco was already unpopular with the Leeds fans, as he had his every touch booed for his antics in the summer against England.

He left Stamford Bridge popular with the home supporters though, with his 80th-minute strike securing the Blues’ fifth and final goal.

Sports.title: Arsenal ratings: Odegaard’s sensational start to season continues at Napoli but Gyokeres is miles off the pace
Sports.content:
MARTIN ODEGAARD continued his incredible start to the season as he fired Arsenal to a win in their Champions League opener.

The Gunners edged a 1-0 win over Napoli to get their European campaign underway with three points.



Mikel Arteta‘s side dominated the ball and played patient attacking football as they waited for the right moment to pounce.

That came when captain Odegaard let fly from outside the area and broke the deadlock late in the second half.



Odegaard was the star of the show for most of the game, marking his fifth goal contribution in as many games this season.

Here’s how SunSport Arsenal Reporter Joshua Hall rated each individual Arsenal performance…

DAVID RAYA – 7

Uncharacteristically spilled Kevin De Bruyne’s powerful effort in the first half, but was solid with his shot-stopping throughout.

His distribution seems to have gone up another level this season and he was firing the ball to Arsenal shirts at every opportunity.

BEN WHITE – 7

Jurrien Timber travelled with the Arsenal team to Naples, but was still absent from the matchday squad, meaning White will be keeping his starting spot at right-back for a little while longer.

This was another solid performance from the 28-year-old, who isn’t going to be replaced without putting up a fight.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

EZRI KONSA – 8

There was understandably a lot of concern when news of William Saliba‘s back injury spread this summer, but Konsa has stepped into his shoes with ease.

Arteta has spoken in the past about “plug-and-play” signings and Konsa is showing that with his performances already.

This was another top showing from the former Aston Villa man, who looks dominant when he is called into action.

GABRIEL MAGALHAES – 8

Impressive as ever and adapting really well to playing alongside a new partner in Konsa.



The Brazilian made a crucial intervention to deny Kevin De Bruyne when the Napoli midfielder was bursting into the box.

PIERO HINCAPIE – 6

A first start of the season for the Ecuador international, who has a big task on his hands if he wants to keep in-form Riccardo Calafiori out of the team going forward.

Tried to make his mark with a cross-cum-shot that almost crept in, but was unable to pull off a miraculous goal.

He will be kicking himself for firing a golden opportunity over the bar early in the second half that should have been a guaranteed goal.



DECLAN RICE – 7

Rice has become ‘Mr. Reliable’ for Mikel Arteta ever since his arrival at the club in 2023 – this was another of those commanding performances.

The midfielder was so calm in his own box to prevent Napoli a goal in the first half and offered threat going forward too.

MIKEL MERINO – 7

Always drifting into the box and trying to impact the game like he has done so many times before.

There will be questions about if he should have done better when his first-half header was saved from point blank range.



But perhaps that is a sign of a player starting his first game in months.

MARTIN ODEGAARD – 9

The Norwegian has started the season on fire, using his World Cup campaign as a catalyst for his club form.

This game was no different as his dancing feet and remarkable vision played a part in almost every Arsenal attack.

But after nobody else could finish it off, it was his long-range bullet that found the back of the net and finally rewarded Arsenal for their patient play.



BUKAYO SAKA – 6

Not his usual clinical self despite working into a host of brilliant positions throughout the game.

He will be frustrated with how he made a hash of a huge opportunity when he was played through by Odegaard.

The linesman’s flag spared his blushes despite there being no offside in the build-up.



EBERE EZE – 6

Eze is going to have to play a lot more football on the left flank this season after the departures of Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli.

The England international drifted in and out of the game and struggled to come up with the goods when he did have the ball at his feet.

Ultimately replaced by Christos Tzolis.

VIKTOR GYOKERES – 6

Arteta has trusted Kai Havertz in his opening four games this season, but finally gave Gyokeres the nod from the off in Naples.

The striker was largely anonymous, but it is hard to blame him given the way that Napoli set up so deep in their own half.



You have to wonder if Arteta should have stuck to his guns and played Havertz up top, particularly after his masterclass against Chelsea at the weekend.

The German did replace Havertz in the 73rd minute.

SUBSTITUTES

BRUNO GUIMARAES (for Merino, 65 mins) – 7

Another impressive substitute cameo from the Brazilian, who looks hungry to make an impact at Arsenal.



CHRISTOS TZOLIS (for Eze, 65 mins) – 7

Lashed at his chance inside the box as he tried to make an instant impact off the bench.

But managed to register an assist as he made the final pass to Odegaard for the game’s only goal.

NONI MADUEKE (for Saka, 73 mins) – 6

Had to do so much better when he was played through one-on-one against the goalkeeper by Havertz late on.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

KAI HAVERTZ (for Gyokeres, 73 mins) – 7

His technical ability is a level above Gyokeres and it is evident whenever he gets the ball.

Thought he had tucked home a goal of his own in injury time, but was called offside.



MARTIN ZUBIMENDI (for White, 82 mins) – N/A

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola gives immediate Bradley Barcola injury update after Liverpool win
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola gives immediate Bradley Barcola injury update after Liverpool win

Liverpool were worried after £123million summer signing Bradley Barcola went off in the second half of their win over Atletico Madrid with an apparent calf injury

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola went down holding his calf (Image: Richard Sellers/Getty Images)

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola admitted he was relieved when Bradley Barcola told him he was only suffering with cramp after coming off against Atletico Madrid.

‌



Barcola started the 2-1 win at Anfield on Wednesday night but was forced off in the 60 minute. The £123million summer signing went down holding his left calf after sprinting in behind the defence.

‌



The Frenchman missed two brilliant chances to get off the mark in a Liverpool shirt. And the sight of him being treated by the medical staff on the pitch before gingerly walking off would have worried the Liverpool supporters.

‌



Iraola was spotted nervously asking Barcola if it was just cramp as he came off to the substitutes' bench. And the Liverpool boss confirmed the good news in an interview with TNT Sports after the final whistle.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Alexis Mac Allister backs up contract demand as Liverpool beat Atletico - 5 talking points READ MORE :

"It was just cramps, especially with Bradley [Barcola]. We are rushing him, he hasn't played any minutes in pre-season, but today we decided to ask him to give everything he had," Iraola said. "Let's see how they recover for the next one."

‌



Liverpool found themselves 1-0 down early on when Marcos Llorente raced onto Julian Alvarez's through ball and beat Alisson one-on-one. But they levelled through Dominik Szoboszlai's cool finish from close range and then pulled ahead through a rocket from Alexis Mac Allister.

Barcola had two good chances to open his account for his new club, but couldn't take them. His first effort was saved by Jan Oblak moments before Szoboszlai's goal, while his second was put wide when clean through on goal.

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola started on the right wing for Liverpool before going off with cramp (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



Iraola was pleased with the way that his side responded after being caught by surprise by Diego Simeone's tactical set-up. "Difficult to ask for more. We showed character. I loved the second half. I feel lucky to experience this atmosphere," he said.

"I think I have to take blame from the beginning because they surprised me a little bit tactically they played a five at the back, a 5-3-2. We expected something different and waited to correct it. After half-time, we had a much better game, we pressed better, and I think we have been the better team."

Sports.title: Ryan Giggs sends JJ Gabriel a clear warning despite comparison with Man Utd legend
Sports.content:
Ryan Giggs sends JJ Gabriel a clear warning despite comparison with Man Utd legend

Manchester United wonderkid JJ Gabriel has a huge amount of hype around him and club legend Ryan Giggs has sent the 15-year-old some advice after an exciting pre-season

View 3 Images Ryan Giggs has given some advice to JJ Gabriel (Image: Rio Ferdinand Presents)

Ryan Giggs believes JJ Gabriel is a "generational talent" who reminds him of Wayne Rooney, but he's urged the Manchester United youngster to remain patient for his first-team breakthrough.

‌



Gabriel has a huge amount of hype around him, having caught the eye of United's coaches and their supporters at the tender age of 15. He made his maiden first-team appearance against Atletico Madrid in pre-season and could become United's youngest ever debutant in the coming weeks.

‌



Gabriel doesn't turn 16 until October 6, meaning he has plenty of time to beat the record held by goalkeeper David Gaskell, who was 16 years and 19 days when he made his debut for United.

‌



He has been starring for United's under-21s recently and there is a clamour for Michael Carrick to thrust him into the spotlight when United play Brighton in the Carabao Cup next week.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Giggs knows all about what Gabriel is facing, having first trained with the United first team at the age of 15 before making his debut aged 17. The legendary United winger discussed his prospects with ex-teammate Rio Ferdinand on his YouTube channel.

"It was really interesting to see how they're integrating the young players into the squad," Ferdinand said on The Debrief, reflecting on a training session he witnessed in Dublin this summer. "Shea Lacey, the Fletcher twins, JJ Gabriel. I watched a session, a small-sided game. Off both feet, he's ridiculous - getting a yard and bang.

"So small and slight but doesn't allow people contact. He did a shooting drill... imagine being 15 on the training pitch with the PFA Player of the Year, captain of your club, best player at your club (Bruno Fernandes) - and you and him are the focal point of a shooting drill in front of everybody. And he's looking comfortable and unfazed.

‌



View 3 Images JJ Gabriel is the most exciting player in Manchester United's academy (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

"Forget his ability, just his mental ability to put the noise out the way and do something like that. My head would've been gone. I remember being called over to the first-team training pitch when I was 17 or 18 and I was like 'gather yourself, get your thoughts together' but he just looked calm, it was unreal."

Giggs: "That sounds like Wayne, doesn't it?"

‌



Ferdinand: "Yeah, the mindset."

Giggs: "Just give me the ball, give me the ball, I don't care who I'm training with."

Giggs then went on to give Gabriel some advice, stating "sometimes you have to be patient".

‌



View 3 Images Wayne Rooney made an immediate impact at Manchester United as a youngster (Image: PA)

"You need to play games and it's difficult because if you're in squads for the first team you're not going to turn that down, but also you need minutes on the pitch," he explained. "A couple of times I went up to the first team and then went back to the youth team - and it's about how you react to that. Are they still showing that same ability when they go back?

"He's at the best club because of the history of young players coming through and how they're looked after. He's got good people around him who have played at the club - Michael Carrick, Darren Fletcher, Jonny Evans.

Article continues below

"It's sort of a generational talent, so there's no point going out on loan because he's at the best place. He'll be dipping in and out of the first team so that experience is invaluable - not only the games and the training, but also travelling with the team and managing the expectation of United. The focus is so huge on Manchester United and you need to get used to that."

Sports.title: Declan Rice reaches Premier League title agreement with young Arsenal fan
Sports.content:
Declan Rice reaches Premier League title agreement with young Arsenal fan

Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice has promised to dye his hair with red highlights if the Gunners successfully defend their Premier League title this season

View Image Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice (Image: Getty Images)

Declan Rice has promised to dye his hair with red highlights if Arsenal win the Premier League title again. The Gunners romped to their first top flight in 22 years last season with Rice featuring in all-but two of their league fixtures as Mikel Arteta's side finished seven points ahead of runners-up Manchester United.

‌



Arsenal are the bookmakers' favourites to win the title this season and have enjoyed a perfect start, earning three straight wins and conceding just one goal in the process. They kicked off their campaign with a 3-0 triumph over Coventry City and have subsequently followed that up by beating Aston Villa 1-0 and Chelsea 2-1.

‌



It's a start that leaves them in second in the Premier League table, the same as City, though Enzo Maresca's side occupy top spot having scored one more goal. Hull City, meanwhile, have been the surprise package and sit third on seven points, with Chelsea are in fourth on six points and Brentford rounding out the top five on five points.

‌



Julian Alvarez 'suffering' after failed Arsenal transfer as statement made before Liverpool READ MORE :

Diego Simeone makes honest Julian Alvarez admission ahead of Liverpool clash READ MORE :

Earlier this week, England midfielder Rice was questioned by a young Arsenal supporter about whether he would dye his hair should the Gunners claim the Premier League crown again. When Rice pushed back to ask what colour they had in mind, the fan enthusiastically replied: "Red and white."

Rice then decided to propose a compromise to the supporter, stating he would be willing to have "red highlights in" should Arsenal win the title for the second successive season.

After the fan accepted the arrangement, Rice concluded: "Yes. Buzzing."

‌

Having secured maximum points from their opening three Premier League fixtures, Arsenal now shift their focus to the Champions League, with the Gunners set to face Napoli on Wednesday.

Ahead of the trip to the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, Arteta said: "I'm really excited. We know what this competition means to all of us, the experience of last year as well, so we need to start with the first game in a really, really tough place, but really excited to start the campaign.

"Start well tomorrow; that's the only thing we can do. Start by putting in a big performance tomorrow to increase the probability of winning the game."

Sports.title: Rory McIlroy opens up on 'bad habits' and vows to change before Donald Trump visit
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy opens up on 'bad habits' and vows to change before Donald Trump visit

Rory McIlroy has been brutally honest about the state of his game at the moment and pledged to make some big chances before his Irish Open defence

View 3 Images Rory McIlroy is getting ready for his Irish Open title defence (Image: Richard Heathcote, Getty Images)

Rory McIlroy has made it clear there are many "bad habits" he must iron out before his Irish Open defence. Since he retained the Masters, McIlroy has admitted there are inconsistencies in his game, particularly with his swing.

‌



This weekend, he has the opportunity to correct all of those and show his best form at his home tournament, which will be attended by US president Donald Trump.

‌



Last year, McIlroy won the competition in stunning fashion. He holed a 25-foot putt for an eagle in the 72nd hole to force a play-off with Swedish ace Joakim Lagergren, before eventually sealing the victory in the third hole.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

McIlroy has not won a tournament since retaining the Masters this year, with his best display coming in last month's BMW Championship, where he placed third.

Discussing the recent struggles he has experienced with his swing, the Northern Irishman said: "I played Memphis (FedEx St Jude Championship) and played very poorly, and was looking at my swing on video and just didn't like where it was. I submitted to making a few changes - not changes that are unfamiliar to me, changes that I have had to do before.

‌



"Everyone has their tendencies and bad habits in the golf swing and I just got into a bad habit in mine. It is still something I am working through and conscious of, but I do think if I can really dig into it in the next few months, I feel like I will start the 2027 year where I want it to be.

View 3 Images McIlroy was brutally honest about his performance after his disappointment in Memphis (Image: Icon Sportswire, Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

"I think everyone's golf course is a work-in-progress - mine is no different. There is always things that you want to try to improve upon."

‌



McIlroy finished 66th in Memphis after carding eight over par, a massive 25 strokes adrift of eventual champion Scottie Scheffler. Following the tournament, he confessed to feeling "lost" with his swing, sparking worry amongst supporters of the game.

At the time, he said: "Obviously didn't come in here with a ton of reps, almost felt like the more the week went on, the more I felt lost with my golf swing a little bit.

View 3 Images McIlroy opened up about the improvements he has made to his swing (Image: Richard Heathcote, Getty Images)

Article continues below

"I figured it out a little bit the last few holes today, I think. Yeah, swing wasn't in sync and obviously didn't do a ton of practice coming in here.

"I guess nice to shake the rust off a little bit, but I'm going to have to work pretty hard between now and next Thursday to feel like I have any sort of golf game to compete next week."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel should break unwritten rule for inspirational West Ham captain Jarrod Bowen
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel should break unwritten rule for inspirational West Ham captain Jarrod Bowen

Jarrod Bowen stayed with the Hammers despite their relegation to the Championship and has helped his side move to the top of the table after the opening six games of the season

View 3 Images Jarrod Bowen is leading West Ham by example in the Championship (Image: West Ham United FC/West Ham United FC via Getty Images)

It has become accepted football wisdom that Championship players should not make the England grade. Goalkeepers might have an outside chance because of a small pool of number ones in the Premier League, but not outfield players.

‌



The last Championship footballer to play a match for England was Sam Johnstone, who was West Bromwich Albion’s keeper when he earned three England caps in 2021. James Trafford earned a call-up from Thomas Tuchel when playing for Burnley in the Championship but did not make his debut until he was on Manchester City’s books.

‌



Since he became England manager, it is unlikely Tuchel has been to a Championship match. But he does not need to go to a match to make an exception to the Championship rule when he names his latest squad next week.

‌



He is unlikely to do it, but Tuchel should include Jarrod Bowen. And not just because his form has been predictably good for West Ham, not just because he scored a couple in the 3-2 win at Bolton the other night.

But because he bucked a trend. Because he showed qualities that are important in a character representing his country. Loyalty, spirit.

Bowen has suddenly not become below international class because he has played his last six matches in the Championship. He was very unlucky not to make Tuchel’s squad for the World Cup, don’t forget.

‌



Bowen has not stayed at West Ham purely out of love. He is extremely well-remunerated and perhaps there was not as much elite interest in him as might have been expected before he made his decision to remain at the club.

View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel will name his latest England squad next week (Image: Getty Images)

And it is a calculated gamble. Bowen might have realised this could be a thoroughly enjoyable season.

‌



He might have realised that being relegated from the Premier League does not need to be the doomsday scenario that so many like to imagine. West Ham fans might already be having more fun than they had in the entirety of last season.

They will see more goals - West Ham are averaging 2.3 a game as opposed to 1.2 a game last season - and they will see more wins. They will enjoy going to places such as Bolton. It makes a change. They will revel in the challenge of returning to the top flight.

View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel left Jarrod Bowen out of his World Cup squad (Image: Getty Images)

‌



They will see their team have the ball a lot more than they did last season. And they will not have to put up with the royal pain that VAR has become.

There is not a massive amount not to like. And, in their massive numbers, they will have a fantastic bond with a player who - after six and a half years at the club - has become one of their own.

Tuchel should not be in the business of handing out rewards to players just because they are nice guys. But Bowen is a very good player who is taking on a different challenge. And that should not mean his England career is put on hold.

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp in Trent Alexander-Arnold agreement with Jose Mourinho as boss issues verdict
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp in Trent Alexander-Arnold agreement with Jose Mourinho as boss issues verdict

Trent Alexander-Arnold has forced Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho to reach a verdict - and it's a sentiment long echoed by Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp

View 3 Images Trent Alexander-Arnold's performance in midfield for Real Madrid has made up Jose Mourinho's mind (Image: Getty)

Trent Alexander-Arnold was trialled in midfield by Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho on Tuesday evening. But the Portuguese manager has reached the same conclusion as former Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp: Alexander-Arnold is better as a right-back.

‌



Since moving to the Bernabeu last summer, the English defender has struggled with injuries. He did, however, make 35 appearances last term, registering five assists. Alas, with Mourinho's arrival came more roadblocks, as the ex-Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham boss sanctioned the signing of a new right-back.

‌



Netherlands international Denzel Dumfries has arrived from Inter Milan for £17million. In pre-season, Mourinho tried to play Alexander-Arnold alongside his new team-mate. In the Champions League on Tuesday evening, Inter Milan witnessed a brand new experiment.

‌



With Dumfries selected in defence to face his old club, former Liverpool vice-captain Alexander-Arnold was deployed in midfield. He had previously filled that role under Gareth Southgate for England, but this latest trial proved relatively ineffective despite the Spanish giants claiming a 2-1 victory.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Jose Mourinho makes thoughts clear on Trent Alexander-Arnold experiment READ MORE :

Jamie Carragher leaves Micah Richards in stitches with bankruptcy joke on live TV READ MORE :

Alexander-Arnold featured for 79 minutes before making way for Aurelien Tchouameni , and Mourinho has reached the same conclusion as Klopp: Alexander-Arnold is firmly a right-back, not a midfielder.

‌



His deployment in midfield was partially driven by Real Madrid's shortage of options in the centre of the pitch. Eduardo Camavinga, Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva were all unavailable due to UEFA carry-over suspensions.

View 3 Images Mourinho spoke out about the English star after the win (Image: Getty)

Watch Liverpool vs Atlético Madrid on TNT Sports This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more from £25.99 TNT Sports Get TNT Sports here Product Description Liverpool host Atlético Madrid in their opening Champions League fixture on September 9 . Fans can watch the game live on TNT Sports via HBO Max or Prime Video's TNT Sports channel.

‌



Whilst Mourinho praised the player, he made a significant admission: "He has played midfield with England and Liverpool... But he is not a midfielder.

"He has played very well. He has interpreted what he needed to really well, tactically. Both him and [Federico] Valverde have worked very well at this level."

In 2023, during a Premier League fixture against Fulham, Alexander-Arnold, who had been operating as an inverted full-back, moved into a holding midfield position for the closing 30 minutes of the match. Liverpool secured a 4-3 victory with Alexander-Arnold netting an 88th-minute winner.

‌



However, ex-Reds boss Klopp made it abundantly clear after the final whistle that he did not consider the player a long-term midfield solution. He said: "I'm not stubborn and don't want to play him midfield, not at all, but I am not part of the discussion. You can discuss it as much as you want, but it will not have any influence.

View 3 Images Klopp never considered Trent Alexander-Arnold a midfielder (Image: Getty)

"Yes, Trent can play midfield but we always knew that Trent can play the role we gave him now very well as well. He became one of the most successful players in the history of Liverpool, in the recent history, playing as a right-back. He became a Premier League player as a right-back."

Article continues below

Two years before this, Klopp verbally reached the exact same conclusion as Mourinho has this week. In 2021, England manager Southgate chose to deploy Alexander-Arnold centrally rather than in his usual right-back position during a World Cup qualifier against Andorra.

He managed just 45 minutes there before being switched back to full-back. Klopp was baffled by the decision and told Sky Sports: "Why would you make the best right-back in the world a midfielder? I don't understand that really."

Sports.title: Man City and Premier League 'braced for £100m bill' as huge claim made about 115 charges case
Sports.content:
Man City and Premier League 'braced for £100m bill' as huge claim made about 115 charges case

The Premier League's legal battle with Manchester City has still not seen a result and has been ongoing for almost two years since the 12-week hearing finished in 2024

View 2 Images The outcome of the Premier League's legal battle with Manchester City is still unknown (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Manchester City and the Premier League's legal battle is estimated to have cost each over £100m and may have already reached the appeal stage, according to football finance expert Kieran Maguire. City were charged with 115 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules in February 2023, but no result has been forthcoming.

‌



Maguire, who admits he has no evidence to support such a suspicion, said he would not be surprised if one party were appealing an initial finding, given the silence around the case. He highlighted a similar situation with Chelsea, where the news did not emerge until after their appeal over 78 charges.

‌



A 12-week hearing into the charges against City concluded in December 2024. With the two-year mark approaching, the independent commission is yet to publish a ruling on the complex case, with City strongly denying the allegations they face.

‌



"We are probably talking hundreds and hundreds of thousands of pieces of evidence, and they have to be gone through with a fine-tooth comb," Maguire said on the Rest is Football podcast.

"We saw with the Chelsea case, where Chelsea had 78 charges, that the verdict was given and Chelsea effectively appealed and that took another 3 or 4 months to work out.

‌



"So we could be in a situation, and I have no evidence to back this up, that there has been a decision made on Manchester City and either the Premier League or Manchester City have immediately appealed and we are now actually working out way through the appeal process to get a final, final answer. We didn't know that (there was an appeal) in terms of Chelsea."

Mirror Sport have approached Manchester City and the Premier League for comment.

In May, it was suggested that a result could still be two years away. The scale of the charges and the severity of the accusations have ensured a long wait for an unprecedented case in English football.

‌



Among City's charges are 54 allegations of failing to provide accurate and up-to-date financial information from 2009 until 2018. They also face 14 alleged breaches of failing to provide accurate financial reports of player and manager compensation over the same period.

View 2 Images Manchester City were handed 115 charges over three years ago. (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"We are now almost two years since the commission first sat, it commenced in September 2024," Maguire said. "It took around about 10-12 weeks to hear all the evidence. As one lawyer said to me, if there are 115 charges, there are 115 defences, so it makes it difficult.

"You have got three people sitting on the commission, all of whom are very high-powered people in their own right, so getting them into the same room at the same time over the course of the last 18-20 months has proven to be very difficult.

"Then, from what I understand and there has been very much a news blackout, you have got to give the people and professionals involved a lot of credit. There are no leaks, no WhatsApp groups with gossip."

‌

The wait is proving costly for both the Premier League and City, however. Maguire believes both will have racked up nine-figure bills.

"These charges are so serious that it is difficult to see how the board of Manchester City could survive if they lose the case and it would be hugely embarrassing for the Premier League if they lose the case because the legal costs for both parties are probably in excess of £100m," Maguire added.

‌



Premier League chief Richard Masters has admitted that the process has taken longer than he hoped. Speaking last month he suggested he was unable to provide an update and that the system must be allowed to take its course.

"Our rules are very clear about that - I have to keep everything confidential until we're ready to hand down a decision and be clear about it," he said. "I can't give any update on timing or what's happening.

"There's only one available route through this, which is to allow the process to take its course. It has taken longer than expected, and I do understand the frustrations."
